title: Nonuniform three-dimensional J2 bending path
purpose: Verify that the global J2 transaction, consistent tangent, prescribed-motion work, energy accounting, and result recovery remain coherent when a structural model contains elastic and plastified integration points simultaneously.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises plasticity with linear isotropic hardening under displacement-controlled bending

execution.evidence: A slender tetrahedral cantilever is clamped at one end and translated transversely at the other through eight accepted increments, producing a mixed elastic/plastic integration-point state.

observables: Minimum, maximum, and range of committed equivalent plastic strain.
Number of plastified integration points relative to the complete quadrature identity.
Prescribed-motion external work, internal energy, and their balance error.
Quadrature S/PE/PEEQ/MISES plus recovered cell fields and nodal RF.
acceptance: Some but not all integration points are plastic at the final state.
PEEQ is nonuniform and remains nonnegative.
External work and internal energy are positive and their relative difference remains below eight percent for the declared eight-increment path.
limitations: This is an internal structural regression rather than an independent external validation.
The coarse cantilever is designed to exercise state localization and energy plumbing, not to report a converged beam response.
The official Abaqus notched-beam comparison remains a separate external benchmark gate.
